jobs.prompt:
refactor(cpp): finish the llhttp fetch-response work: body framing on llhttp, fetch tests on standard behaviour

CONTEXT (you have no other context than this prompt and the repository)
You start from branch `agent-jobs/cppgw-std-llhttp-client-r1-44201999462-1` of ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi: a known-good state of `cpp/gateway/`, a C++20 port of this repository's TypeScript gateway (`src/`, `serve.ts`), with a JavaScript-style runtime layer (`include/uos/rt`, `src/rt`, `src/runtime`), vendored simdjson and simdutf (`cpp/gateway/third_party/`), ICU for Unicode, and about 442 standalone test binaries (`cpp/gateway/tests/**/*_test.cpp`). On this state the release build passes its whole suite on Linux ARM64. The native gateway is already 1.2-1.9x faster than the TypeScript gateway on Bun end to end and uses about a third of the memory (`cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-perf-request-path-20261117.md`). Every deployment target is 64-bit ARM: an Arch Linux ARM VPS, an Apple Silicon Mac and a Raspberry Pi.

OWNER POLICY (binding): generic functionality comes from mature open-source or standard libraries; exact parity with Bun's quirks and error wording is NOT required; less first-party code is preferred. What must hold: the gateway's functional behaviour (wire formats, status codes, stored data, authentication and validation decisions, accounting) and security never getting weaker.

READ FIRST: `cpp/gateway/docs/CI.md` (portable build-and-test driver; invoke it as `bash cpp/gateway/tools/ci-build.sh ...`, the file lacks its executable bit), `cpp/gateway/docs/BUILD.md`, `cpp/gateway/docs/RUNTIME.md`, `cpp/gateway/docs/OSS-REPLACEMENT-PLAN.md`, `cpp/gateway/PORTING.md` (its coroutine rules are mandatory; its "Host safety" and "compile only through tools/unit.sh" rules apply to the authors' server, not to your disposable runner; where it demands exact Bun parity, the owner policy above wins). `python3 cpp/gateway/tools/links.py <test>` prints a test's application sources; every `src/rt/*.cpp` and the vendored libraries link into every test.

About ten other agents are changing other parts of `cpp/gateway` on their own branches at the same time (URL, HTTP parsing, regex, WebSocket, passkey CBOR and ASN.1, BigInt, date/console/filesystem/env/headers helpers, the stored-value reader, a test-suite repair). Your branch will be merged with theirs: stay strictly inside your OWNED PATHS and keep everything else byte-identical.

GENERAL RULES
- The runner holds a model gateway token: never print it or write any credential to a file. Run tests with an empty `HOME`, a fresh `TMPDIR` and no provider variables. No real provider traffic: use local mocks only.
- Do not edit `.github/` (unless your task says so), the TypeScript, or `cpp/` outside `cpp/gateway/`. Do not delete or weaken tests.
- Model connections can drop: create your report file in the first minutes and commit small steps often (the tree must build at each commit). Leave no build output, binaries or downloads in the checkout.
- Report file: `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/<job id>.md`: what you did, exact commands, real counts and measurements, what is unfinished, defects found outside your paths (report, do not fix). End your final message with the same summary.

YOUR MACHINE: GitHub-hosted Linux ARM64 runner (Ubuntu 24.04, 4 CPUs, 16 GB, sudo, network). Its packages are too old for this tree: install Clang 21 or newer from apt.llvm.org (or GCC 14+), build Boost 1.92.0 `json` and `container` static libraries from the official source archive in a temp directory (the tree needs Boost >= 1.86), install OpenSSL 3, zlib, ICU, brotli, zstd development packages and build SQLite 3.54.0 as `cpp/gateway/docs/CI.md` describes. Bun 1.4.0 may be installed when you need to run the TypeScript.

OWNED PATHS (you may create or edit only these, plus your report)
- `cpp/gateway/src/rt/fetch_transport_http.cpp`, `cpp/gateway/src/rt/fetch_transport_internal.hpp`, `cpp/gateway/src/rt/fetch_transport.cpp` (only the response body pump and its call into the parser), the fetch tests under `cpp/gateway/tests/rt/` and `cpp/gateway/tests/` whose names start with `fetch` (expectations only, per the policy), `cpp/gateway/fuzz/fetch_response_library.cpp`, `cpp/gateway/docs/DEVIATIONS-FROM-BUN.md` (append), `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-std-llhttp-client-20261117.md` (append)

TASK
This branch already contains an earlier agent's work (read `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-std-llhttp-client-20261117.md` first): fetch response heads, chunked bodies and the WebSocket client's handshake head are parsed by llhttp 9.4.4 (vendored under `cpp/gateway/third_party/llhttp/`). It reported 440 of 442 binaries passing on ARM64 and left three things undone because they were outside its allowed paths. Do them:
1. Two fetch test binaries still assert Bun-era behaviour (exact error wording and leniencies of Bun's own response parser). Find them (build and run the tests whose link lists include `src/rt/fetch_transport_http.cpp`), and for each failing assertion decide per the owner policy: a FUNCTIONAL property (a response a real HTTP server can send must still be accepted; status, headers and body bytes delivered intact; errors surface as the port's ordinary fetch error type; malformed or ambiguous framing such as conflicting Content-Length/Transfer-Encoding is REJECTED) must hold, fix the code if it does not; wording or Bun-specific leniency: change the expectation and record the class in `DEVIATIONS-FROM-BUN.md`.
2. The live response body pump still counts fixed-length bytes and detects end-of-stream itself. Let llhttp drive body framing (content-length, chunked, close-delimited, HEAD/204/304/1xx no-body cases) through its callbacks and delete the duplicate first-party bookkeeping.
3. The earlier agent measured short server-sent-event responses getting SLOWER (462 -> 661 ns/op) while handshake parsing got faster. Profile that path, remove the overhead (per-chunk parser re-initialisation, copies between the parser callbacks and the stream, per-event allocations), and report before/after; it must end at or below the pre-llhttp 462 ns/op, or you explain precisely what prevents it.

DONE WHEN
Every test whose link list includes the fetch transport passes in release and under ASan+UBSan on your ARM64 runner, the full suite passes (`bash cpp/gateway/tools/ci-build.sh --config release`, all shards), and the report has the SSE before/after numbers and first-party lines removed.
